name: Chip supply
summary: Helium shortage from Hormuz disruption; China's rare-earth pause ends 10 Nov
state: Qatar supplies a large share of the world's helium, which chip fabs need, and Hormuz disruption plus China's July helium export ban have tightened supply. China's rare-earth export pause expires on 10 Nov. TSMC shares fell 1.5% on 2 Nov amid volatile tech trading, but no major TSMC or Samsung output stoppage had been reported.
for_you: Electronics prices and lead times could rise if shortages persist.
rubric_hit: Shortages reported in a key input (helium) = Watch

why: Advanced chips underpin everything from phones to AI to weapons; supply is concentrated in Taiwan and Korea.
drivers: Export controls, Taiwan risk, fab outages, AI demand, materials.

rubric.alert: Major disruption to TSMC/Samsung output, or controls halting a major supply chain.
rubric.watch: New export controls, shortages reported in key segments, or a fab outage.
rubric.normal: Supply normal; no new major controls.
